biodiversity_overview.text: 3,963 GBIF occurrence records for 30 tracked species are attributed to Arunachal Pradesh, spanning 1986-2026.
3,898 of these records (98.4%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 13, Magnoliopsida 7, Mammalia 6, Amphibia 2, Squamata 1, Actinopterygii 1.

threatened_species.text: 1 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
3 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Asian Elephant (EN), Tiger (EN), Indian Rhinoceros (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Cuckoo (2,275), Indian White-eye (834), Indian Blue Robin (266), Indian Pied Starling (254), Indian Paradise-flycatcher (189).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 143 in 2016 to 12 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 10.8% of Arunachal Pradesh's area (15 areas intersect the state).
23.0% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (897 of 3,898); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Spikenard (0.64), Indian Rhinoceros (0.41), Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Indian Grass-babbler (0.30), Bulletwood (0.30).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Arunachal Pradesh (equal-weight reference): cell near 27.375N 93.375E (overall rank 321, median rank across weightings 320); cell near 27.375N 91.875E (overall rank 349, median rank across weightings 352); cell near 28.125N 95.625E (overall rank 474, median rank across weightings 457).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 65,698 km2 (74.88% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

2,834.7 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (4.31% of the 2000 extent; 2.14% in 2015-2024, rank 9 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2017 (193.41 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.08% of land and population density is 19.7 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
9% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
